systemicTransition.warning: Annual equity closes understate intrayear drawdowns. The panel ranks transition risk well, but it contains few independent global crash clusters and no historical AI-capex analogue.

reverseStress.condition: AI trust break; probabilities are conditional, not current-trajectory odds

variables.aiTrust: 0–1 index; exogenous scenario trigger plus endogenous funding feedback
variables.marginCallPressure: 0–1 index activated by incremental collateral loss
variables.liquidityStress: 0–1 shared state driven by coverage, margin calls and Treasury-sale pressure
variables.cashFlowCoverage: operating cash generation / sticky commitment burden
variables.treasurySalePressure: 0–1 foreign-official sale stress, not a forecast of intent

classification.usSystemic: Bernoulli draw from calibrated banking-crisis transition, updated by simulated liquidity, coverage and China stress.
classification.chinaCrisis: Latent threshold driven by capital outflow, property/LGFV balance-sheet stress, refinancing cost, shared liquidity and US crisis feedback.
classification.joint: Both flags occur on the same path by 2028.

feedbackLoops: AI trust ↓ → revenue coverage ↓ → marginal funding rate ↑
equities ↓ → collateral loss → margin calls/liquidations ↑ → market liquidity ↓ → equities ↓
liquidity ↓ + China risk ↑ → capital outflow ↑ → LGFV refinancing premium ↑
China outflow/fiscal stress → Treasury-sale pressure ↑ → US liquidity/term premium ↑
China crisis raises US systemic transition risk; US systemic stress raises China crisis risk
US/China demand ↓ → EU recession first; reallocation benefit appears only later
warning: The banking-crisis transition is statistically calibrated. China and cross-border elasticities are transparent stress-test parameters, not separately identified causal estimates.
